item.title: Put aside political differences and help those in need this Diwali – Prasad
item.description: As families across Fiji celebrate Diwali today, National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad is urging people to put aside their political differences and remember those struggling with the rising cost of living and ongoing dry conditions. In his Diwali message, Professor Prasad says many families are facing financial difficulties and may not be able to celebrate the Festival of Lights
item.content:encoded:
As families across Fiji celebrate Diwali today, National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad is urging people to put aside their political differences and remember those struggling with the rising cost of living and ongoing dry conditions.

In his Diwali message, Professor Prasad says many families are facing financial difficulties and may not be able to celebrate the Festival of Lights in the same way as others.

He says Diwali is a time to show kindness, share what people have and support those in need.

Professor Prasad also raises concerns about the drought affecting communities across Fiji and encourages people to check on neighbours who may be struggling with water shortages and other difficulties.

He says Fiji's cultural and religious diversity should bring people together rather than divide them.

Professor Prasad stresses that political differences should never damage friendships or relationships within communities.

He says Fiji has experienced enough division in its history, and people must work together to build a country where everyone feels respected and safe.

The NFP Leader is encouraging Fijians to use Diwali as an opportunity to rebuild friendships, settle differences and support families facing hardship.

Prasad says the true message of Diwali is about kindness, respect, unity and looking after one another.

He has also extended his Diwali greetings to everyone celebrating, wishing families peace, happiness, good health and prosperity.

item.title: Diwali brings hope and togetherness to families in Bocalevu
item.description: The spirit of Diwali is bringing hope, love and togetherness to families in Bocalevu, Labasa, as residents come together to celebrate the festival of lights today. Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirijan Prasad says Diwali is one of the biggest and most important celebrations in the Hindu religion, representing love, care, forgiveness and unity.
item.content:encoded:
The spirit of Diwali is bringing hope, love and togetherness to families in Bocalevu, Labasa, as residents come together to celebrate the festival of lights today.

Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirijan Prasad says Diwali is one of the biggest and most important celebrations in the Hindu religion, representing love, care, forgiveness and unity.

Prasad says the festival is a time to put differences aside, forgive one another and spread love regardless of race or background.

He says although the drought has dried up local water sources, making preparations difficult, the Water Authority of Fiji delivered water to help families get ready for the celebrations.

He thanked the Authority for its assistance, saying sweets have been prepared and homes are ready for Diwali.

Prasad says families are now looking forward to the Diwali Pooja this afternoon and has wished everyone a happy and blessed Diwali.

item.title: Three traders and three outlets found breaching regulations during Diwali inspections
item.description: Three traders in the Central and Western Divisions have been found breaching the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission Act 2010, while three outlets in the Western Division were found violating food safety regulations during Diwali inspections. The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission says it has intensified inspections across the country during the Diwali festive period .
item.content:encoded:
Three traders in the Central and Western Divisions have been found breaching the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission Act 2010, while three outlets in the Western Division were found violating food safety regulations during Diwali inspections.

The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission says it has intensified inspections across the country during the Diwali festive period .

FCCC says its officers have carried out 184 inspections and surveillance activities, along with 26 joint inspections with health inspectors nationwide.

The Commission says three traders were found breaching regulations relating to the sale of goods without FCCC price authorisation, the sale of price-controlled goods at approved maximum prices and the proper display of prices.

FCCC says three outlets in the Western Division were also found breaching food safety regulations during joint inspections with health inspectors.

The Commission says discoloured meat products and expired food items were condemned during the inspections.

FCCC says its officers are checking whether businesses are clearly displaying prices, charging customers the correct amounts and providing receipts.

Officers are also inspecting food products to ensure they are safe for consumption and have clearly marked expiry dates.

Meanwhile, FCCC is urging shoppers to exercise caution when purchasing items advertised as Diwali specials.

The Commission is reminding consumers to check expiry dates, ensure prices at the checkout match those displayed on shelves and check their receipts before leaving supermarkets.

FCCC says these precautions are important to protect consumers from overcharging and ensure families purchase safe food during the festive season.

item.title: Five Vuniniudrovu families move into safer homes after relocation from high-risk area
item.description: Five families in Vuniniudrovu Village, Naitasiri, have moved into safer homes after being relocated from an area vulnerable to flooding and other natural disasters. The families received their new homes following the completion of the Vuniniudrovu Community Climate Adaptation Facility Relocation Project.
item.content:encoded:
Five families in Vuniniudrovu Village, Naitasiri, have moved into safer homes after being relocated from an area vulnerable to flooding and other natural disasters.

The families received their new homes following the completion of the Vuniniudrovu Community Climate Adaptation Facility Relocation Project.

Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management Mosese Bulitavu officially handed over the homes.

Bulitavu says the families previously lived in a high-risk area classified as a red zone, where they faced threats from heavy rainfall, flooding and other natural disasters.

He says the relocation will provide the families with a safer and more secure living environment.

The project is supported through a partnership between the Fiji Government and the Global Centre for Climate Mobility.

Vuniniudrovu is one of three communities in Fiji, alongside Macuata-i-Wai and Narata, receiving $200,000 each under the programme.

Bulitavu says the relocation is an important step towards protecting vulnerable families from the impacts of climate change.

He is also reminding the families to maintain their new homes to ensure they remain safe and secure in the years ahead.

The Minister is urging the village disaster management committee to remain active and ensure residents are prepared for emergencies.

Bulitavu is also calling on villagers to conserve water as Fiji continues to experience dry conditions, which he links to El Niño.

He says the Government remains committed to supporting vulnerable communities, improving their living conditions and strengthening their ability to prepare for natural disasters and the effects of climate change.

item.title: Special votes could decide who forms New Zealand's next government
item.description: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty over who will form the next government, with special votes expected to determine whether the current coalition retains power. Provisional election results show the incumbent coalition parties, National, ACT and New Zealand First, holding 67 seats, compared to 56 seats for the left bloc, while the Opportunity Party has secured seven seats.
item.content:encoded:
New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty over who will form the next government, with special votes expected to determine whether the current coalition retains power.

Provisional election results show the incumbent coalition parties, National, ACT and New Zealand First, holding 67 seats, compared to 56 seats for the left bloc, while the Opportunity Party has secured seven seats.

However, nearly 600,000 special votes are still to be counted, with final results expected in about three weeks.

The election has also resulted in a larger-than-usual parliamentary overhang, which could increase the number of MPs from the usual 120 to between 129 and 130.

Based on the provisional results, the current coalition could retain power with a narrow majority of just one or two seats.

There are three possible outcomes: National, ACT and New Zealand First could form another coalition government; they could seek support from the Opportunity Party to reach a majority; or Labour, the Greens, Te Pāti Māori and Opportunity could secure enough seats to form a centre-left government.

The final outcome will depend largely on the special votes, which have traditionally favoured left-leaning parties.

Any changes to closely contested electorate seats could also shift the balance of power.

New Zealand's next Parliament must meet by January 14 at the latest, putting pressure on political parties to reach an agreement in the coming weeks.
